role.altitude: The school counselor keeps talking with students, interviewing, judging abilities and next steps, and signing letters; checking credits by hand, scoring paper tests, gathering records and answering the same questions about programs and aid shrink.
skills_to_grow: Checking drafted letters against the facts
role.ambitious_version: A counselor who sees every student at risk of missing a requirement by mid-year and spends the time saved in conversations.

tasks.short: Review transcripts to ensure students meet graduation or entrance requirements, decide follow-up, collect student and teacher input, write letters of recommendation, sign and send them.

steps.what: Counselor reviews transcripts to ensure students meet graduation and entrance requirements
Counselor decides follow-up for students who miss requirements
Student fills in the recommendation questionnaire: activities, goals and achievements
Teachers add short comments on the student to the questionnaire
Counselor writes letters of recommendation

loop.input: The student's questionnaire, teacher comments, grades and the counselor's own notes.
loop.output: A draft letter in the school's format.
loop.check: Every statement must trace to the questionnaire, a comment, a grade or the counselor's notes, and the counselor checks that each statement says what its source says; no health or support-need details; the counselor rewrites the judgement passages.
loop.stop: The counselor signs, or writes the letter by hand after two redrafts.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each letter must read as a personal account of one student.

steps.what: Counselor checks the final letter against the sources and the student's request, and signs it
Counselor sends the signed letter to the college or university

approvals.approved_version: The letter exactly as checked and signed by the counselor in s6, sent once to the college or university named in the student's request; any change needs a new check and signature.

tasks.design: The student information system compares each student's grades and credits with the requirement list of their track and target programs, and lists students who miss something, instead of the counselor checking transcripts one by one. The counselor decides the follow-up. For a letter, the student fills in a short questionnaire and teachers add comments in the same form. A drafting step writes a first letter from these and the counselor's notes, each statement traced to a source; the counselor rewrites, signs and sends it. No software decides eligibility.
tasks.previous_blocker: Transcripts were checked by hand and letters written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Rule checks in student information systems and drafting with source checks.
tasks.still_hard: Students with unusual paths, such as transfers from abroad.
tasks.human_edge: Writing what a teacher saw that no grade shows.

ambition.what: Check requirements every term instead of once in the final year.

tasks.altitude: Less checking and drafting; judgement and signature stay.

reach.learn: Whether students at risk are found earlier.

evidence.claim: Social workers found invented content, including suicidal ideation, in AI-drafted notes.
No decision about a person may rest solely on automated processing.
AI used for admission to education is a high-risk use under the AI Act; here a fixed rule lists gaps and the counselor decides.

assumptions: Boundary: checking requirements and writing recommendation letters; admission decisions are the colleges'.

Input contract for s1: grades and credits recorded by teachers in the student information system, and requirement lists kept by the exam secretary; about 85% of students follow standard tracks; s1 is priced at that share.
Student and teacher time on the questionnaire is shown in s3 and s4 and is outside the counselor's savings.
Follow-up, signing and sending keep their full time.
research_questions: Do fewer students find out late that they miss a requirement?

incremental.description: Counselor keeps the questionnaire and letter format current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: half of students follow non-standard tracks, so s1 keeps 59, and drafts need most passages rewritten, so s5 keeps 90 (17.0); high: 85% standard tracks and drafts as designed (32.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare by reviewing the student's record, encourage students to explore learning opportunities and persevere with challenging tasks, and note the conversation.

steps.what: Counselor reviews the student's record before the conversation
Counselor encourages students to explore learning opportunities and persevere with challenging tasks
Counselor notes the conversation in the student record

tasks.design: A student overview page shows grades, attendance and earlier notes on one screen instead of several tabs. Conversations stay fully personal. The counselor writes the note as today; it is a first record and keeps its time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Student information was spread across tabs.
tasks.enabler_now: Overview pages and note templates in student information systems.
tasks.still_hard: Students who have stopped believing they can succeed.
tasks.human_edge: Finding the one thing a student is proud of.

evidence.claim: Records apps and dashboards fed by the case system replace manual tallies.

assumptions: Boundary: encouragement conversations; counselling for personal problems is outside.
Conversations and notes keep their full time; s1 keeps 70 because reading the record stays and only switching between tabs goes.
research_questions: Are agreed next steps followed up more often?

incremental.description: No new work: the overview page is part of the student information system and needs no upkeep by the counselor.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the overview misses earlier notes kept elsewhere, so s1 keeps 85 (2.2); high: one overview as designed (4.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Administer interest and aptitude tests, score them, gather records, interview the student, evaluate students' abilities, interests and personality characteristics, and write up the evaluation.

steps.what: Counselor administers interest and aptitude tests
Counselor scores the tests against the norm tables
Counselor gathers records: grades, teacher notes and earlier tests
Counselor interviews the student
Counselor evaluates the student's abilities, interests and personality characteristics
Counselor writes up the evaluation in the student record

tasks.design: Students take the school's interest and aptitude tests online in class, and the test platform scores them against its norm tables, so the counselor no longer scores paper tests. A student overview shows grades, teacher notes and earlier test results together. Interviewing and evaluating stay with the counselor; no software judges the student's personality. The evaluation is written in a template in the student record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper tests were scored by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Online career tests with fixed norm scoring and student overview pages.
tasks.still_hard: Students whose test results do not match what they say.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing what a student really wants.
tasks.altitude: Less scoring and gathering; evaluation stays.

reach.learn: Whether shared test results help mentors.

evidence.claim: No decision about a person may rest solely on automated processing.
Online tests can be scored against fixed norm tables without a model.

assumptions: Boundary: evaluating students for study and career choice; diagnosing learning problems is outside.
Input contract for s2: the online test platform licensed by the school scores each test it delivers; paper tests are no longer used.

Interviewing and evaluating keep their full time. s1 keeps 75 because the counselor still runs the session in class; handing out, collecting and sorting paper booklets goes. s6 keeps 85 because the counselor writes the evaluation; the template only fills in scores and grades from the record.
unknowns: Whether the school already uses online tests.
research_questions: Do students start conversations better prepared?

incremental.description: Counselor sets up test sessions on the platform.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: some students still need paper versions of the tests, so about a third are scored by hand (s2 keeps 30) and s1 keeps 90 (20.5); high: all tests online as designed (27.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Keep information on programs, admission, financial aid and apprenticeships current, let students look things up, answer routine questions, provide students with information in conversations and give class presentations.

steps.what: Counselor keeps information on programs, admission requirements and financial aid current in short answer pages
Counselor checks each changed answer page against its official source: dates, requirements, amounts and the link
Counselor publishes the checked answer pages on the school site
Student looks up answers in the school's answer desk

loop.input: The student's question and the counselor's answer pages.
loop.output: A short answer quoting the page it comes from, with the link.
loop.check: Every answer quotes a maintained page and says only what that page says; if no page covers it, the desk says so and offers an appointment. The counselor reads a monthly sample of answers against the quoted pages.
loop.stop: Questions about a student's own situation go to the counselor.
loop.why_not_simpler: Students ask the same thing in many ways.

steps.what: Counselor answers routine questions about programs and deadlines by mail and chat
Counselor provides students with information on degree programs, admission requirements and financial aid in conversations
Counselor gives class presentations on trade and technical schools and apprenticeship programs

tasks.design: The counselor keeps short answer pages on programs, admission, deadlines, financial aid and apprenticeships, linking to the official sources instead of copying them into binders. Students can ask an answer desk on the school site that only quotes these pages, says when it does not know and tells students it is not a person; personal questions go to the counselor. Conversations and presentations stay fully personal.

approvals.approved_version: The changed answer pages exactly as checked by the counselor in s1b, published once on the school site where the answer desk quotes them; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: The same questions came in by mail and were answered one by one.
tasks.enabler_now: Answer desks limited to maintained pages.
tasks.still_hard: Students whose situation does not fit any standard route.
tasks.human_edge: Helping a student see a route they had not considered.

ambition.what: Answer parents' routine questions in the evening, when the counselor is not available.

reach.learn: Whether parents use the answer desk.

evidence.claim: Referral information works best as an answer desk quoting a maintained source, not generated advice.
Staff who use AI systems need sufficient AI literacy.

assumptions: Boundary: information on further education and training; personal counselling is outside.
Input contract for s2: the answer pages kept by the counselor in s1; about half of routine questions are covered; s3 is priced at that share.
Students' time with the answer desk is shown in s2 and is about what writing a mail took.

Conversations, presentations, checking and publishing pages keep their full time. s1 keeps 75 because the counselor writes and updates the pages; linking to official sources removes copying them into binders.
unknowns: Share of questions the pages cover.

incremental.description: Counselor reviews unanswered questions monthly and adds pages.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the pages cover only a quarter of routine questions, so s3 keeps 75 (9.0); high: half covered as assumed (14.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
